title: SchemaRoot
description: Schema vehicle only — never serialised. Carries both wire shapes at the top level of `schema/prophecy.schema.json` so consumers see `Prophecy` and `ProphecySubmission` (and every shared definition) in one file.

ExpiresIn.description: chrono Duration in its serde wire form: [seconds, nanos]

Fulfilment.description: What fulfilling this prophecy means, on a `Prophecy` (§3). `target` and `params` come from the submitter; `requires_human` is **host-stamped** and must not be accepted from a submitter — submitters use [`SubmissionFulfilment`], which has no such field.

params.description: Parameters for the target, from the submitter.

requires_human.description: HOST-STAMPED: true whenever the host accepted a fulfilment with the record, false when the record has none. It has exactly one meaning — *there is a fulfilment to perform* — and is never a trust claim (derivation trust is the host-verified `producer`). A submitter cannot set it.

target.description: A recipe, command or action name the host understands.

Kind.description: What kind of proposal this is. Content is carried by the record's top-level fields (`title`, `body`, `fulfilment`), not by the variant.

oneOf.description: Something observed: a new message, a moved meeting, a changed row. No inference; `confidence` is 1.0 and `fulfilment` is usually absent.
Proposed text. The text lives in `body`; writing it anywhere is the fulfilment, not the prophecy.
A proposed operation: `fulfilment.target` names it, `fulfilment.params` parameterise it.
A proposed change to the producing system itself. A pull request; a human merges it — no host applies it automatically, and a producer never acts on its own.

Producer.description: Who appended the prophecy, as **established by the host** from how the record arrived (in-process reader, verified socket peer, human channel) — never from the record itself.

oneOf.description: Deterministic code, no inference. Readers produce only Findings (§4); a Reader-origin record of any other kind is rejected at append.
A model. May ask for fulfilment; the asking is never the fulfilling. Dismissal by a model is host-opted-in only (§5).
A human — the operator or a reviewer.

Prophecy.description: One prophecy record (§3). Host-stamped fields (`id`, `producer`, `state`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `state_changed_at`, `resolution_note`, `fulfilment.requires_human`) are written by the host and are not accepted from a submitter; submitter fields (`kind`, `source`, `provenance`, `title`, `body`, `confidence`, `fulfilment.target`, `fulfilment.params`) arrive via [`ProphecySubmission`] and are stamped in by [`Prophecy::from_submission`].

body.description: **Submitter-provided.** Full content: for a Draft, the draft text itself; for an Improvement, the proposal and the evidence.

confidence.description: **Submitter-provided.** The producer's own estimate, 0.0–1.0. Readers emit 1.0 (they observed, they did not infer). It is provenance, not a ranking: presentation order is the host's concern and must not be derived from this field alone.

expires_at.description: **Host-stamped** at creation (default 24 h; a submitter may propose a shorter value and the host clamps it). Never extended.

fulfilment.description: **Submitter-provided plan, host-completed.** Present when fulfilling this prophecy means running something; absent for informational Findings.

id.description: **Host-stamped.** Unique, host-assigned (ULID recommended — sortable by creation).

producer.description: **Host-stamped** from the authenticated caller identity (§7.5). A submitter cannot set, propose or override it.

provenance.description: *Submitter-provided.** Capture time plus open evidence map.

resolution_note.description: **Host-stamped.** Required on `Fulfilled` and `Dismissed`; says who decided and why. Machine-written for host bookkeeping (§7.6); a model dismissal carries the model's identity.

source.description: **Submitter-provided.** The configured source plus stable row identity.

state.description: **Host-stamped.** Proposed · Fulfilled · Dismissed · Expired. Only the host changes it (§5).

state_changed_at.description: **Host-stamped.** When `state` last changed — the creation instant while Proposed.

ProphecyId.description: A prophecy's identity. Host-assigned (ULID recommended — sortable by creation); a submitter never provides one.

ProphecySubmission.description: The shape a producer sends to a host (§8): **only submitter fields**. No `id`, no `producer`, no `state`, no `created_at`, no `state_changed_at`, no `requires_human`, no `resolution_note` — the host stamps all of those ([`Prophecy::from_submission`]).

confidence.description: **Submitter-provided.** The producer's own estimate, 0.0–1.0. Readers emit 1.0 (they observed, they did not infer). It is provenance, not a ranking: presentation order is the host's concern and must not be derived from this field alone.

expires_in.description: Proposed expiry. The host clamps it, never extends it; the stamped `expires_at` is the host's word, not the submitter's.

fulfilment.description: **Submitter-provided.** The fulfilment plan minus `requires_human`, which the host stamps.

provenance.description: *Submitter-provided.** Capture time plus open evidence map.

source.description: **Submitter-provided.** The configured source plus stable row identity.

Provenance.description: The audit trail back to what was observed (§3).

evidence.description: An open map the producer fills so the prophecy can be audited back to what was observed. Populo writes `observation_hash` and `event_log_seq`; a repository producer might write a commit id; a chat producer a message id. The schema does not enumerate keys, and no key carries a semantic obligation for consumers. A model-origin record derived from Findings references those Findings' ids here (§6.4); hosts should verify the referenced ids exist.

Source.description: What the producer was looking at: the configured source plus a stable per-row identity (§3).

id.description: The configured source this came from (the host's source id).

row_hash.description: SHA-256, hex-encoded, over the producer's canonical serialisation of the item at observation time. Compared only within one source on one host.

row_key.description: Stable identity of the item across observations, producer-defined (for mail: sender + subject + received; for a calendar: the event's natural key). Deduplication applies only to an identical `(row_key, row_hash)` pair; a changed `row_hash` under the same `row_key` is a content change and produces a NEW prophecy whose evidence references the prior one's id.

State.description: The lifecycle state. All terminal states are terminal: there is no reopening and no second transition (§5).

oneOf.description: Open. Entered at creation; left only by a human decision, host bookkeeping, or expiry.
Terminal. A human approved; the host carries out the fulfilment as ordinary, gated, supervised work.
Terminal. Declined by a human, by host bookkeeping with a machine-written note, or by a model where the host has explicitly opted in (the model's identity is then mandatory in `resolution_note`).
Terminal. `expires_at` passed while still open; the host's sweep moved it here.

SubmissionFulfilment.description: The submitter's form of [`Fulfilment`] (§8): `target` and `params` only. No `requires_human` — the host derives and stamps that.

target.description: A recipe, command or action name the host understands.
